action: Companies offering a self-service data download should check it returns every category of personal data in full, not summaries, and tell users about anything supplied separately. No action needed for Tinder users.
exec: A self-service data export that omits categories of personal data can itself be a GDPR breach; the fine is EUR 11 million.
plain: Ireland's privacy regulator fined the company behind dating app Tinder 11 million euros because its data download tool did not give users all of their personal data.

key_findings: The DPC fined MTCH Technology Services Limited, operator of Tinder, EUR 11 million and issued a reprimand.
The infringement is of GDPR Article 15(3), the right of access to a copy of personal data.
The Download My Data tool omitted some categories of data without notice and gave others only in summary form.
The inquiry was opened by the DPC on its own initiative in January 2020 as MTCH's lead supervisory authority.
recommendations: MTCH must bring its processing into compliance within three months.
Controllers must give people a full copy of their personal data when they exercise the right of access.

summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined MTCH Technology Services Limited, which operates Tinder, EUR 11 million and issued a reprimand. An own-volition inquiry opened in January 2020 found the Download My Data tool did not give users a full copy of their personal data: some categories were left out without notice or supplied only in summary. MTCH must bring its processing into compliance within three months.
title: Irish DPC fines Tinder operator MTCH EUR 11 million over incomplete data access responses

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Irish Data Protection Commission document.
